source.label: U.S. Census 2020, via City Population (Coos County)

budget.adoptedVote: Article 2 on the official ballot on March 10, 2026; the town posted results as a scanned PDF that could not be read, so the outcome is not confirmed.

source.label: Town of Carroll, 2025 Annual Report (2026 warrant and MS-636)

budget.review_note: Warrant amount, not a confirmed result. Election results: https://carrollnh.gov/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/2026-Election-Results.pdf (image only). Article 2 says $3,446,935; the MS-636 total is $3,446,934. The default budget was $3,170,657. The operating figure includes the Water Fund ($340,143 requested for 2026) as well as the General Fund ($3,106,791). The prior-year figure is the MS-636 2025 budget column.

towns.schoolDistrict: White Mountains Regional School District, SAU 36
towns.note: Carroll (Twin Mountain) uses the official ballot (SB 2) system: deliberative session February 3, 2026, ballot voting March 10, 2026. Separate 2026 articles include a $225,000 forestry truck, road work from grants and bond proceeds, a fifth full-time police officer ($66,560 plus $36,343 benefits) and capital reserve deposits; these are not in the operating figure. The town also posted results of a May 26, 2026 special election (not read). The town website posted a White Mountain Regional School District budget hearing notice (January 2, 2026). School district and SAU from Wikipedia's List of school districts in New Hampshire (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_school_districts_in_New_Hampshire), a secondary source.

towns.note: Very small town. Town Meeting: Tuesday, March 10, 2026, 10 a.m., Town Hall. Separate 2026 articles (not in the operating figure) include $50,000 for road paving, $50,000 to the Highway trust fund and $10,000 to the Bridge and Culvert trust fund (both from fund balance), smaller reserve deposits, and $11,000 for a Town Hall conference room. The Conway School District has approved tuition contracts with Albany for Kennett Middle and High School starting in 2027-28 (project schools.json, from SAU 9). SAU from School district and SAU from Wikipedia's List of school districts in New Hampshire (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_school_districts_in_New_Hampshire), a secondary source.
